answer: A trench lock at ocean nadir screens rented keys. A key bonds 2.41 POA and pins a 21-byte nebula wafer. Over 19 hours it sends six 14-byte pulse ticks, 74 minutes apart, each signed from a fresh /22 and folded with the live tip. A descent clerk issues an 11-second nonce bound to the wafer and latest tick. Auditors void a reused /16, ticks under 61 minutes, or two wafers sharing a 7-byte prefix. Four hatches under one wallet in 12 hours, or two wafers sharing three tick prefixes, flood all locks and hold 2.41 POA for 8 epochs. A late nonce or missed tick rusts the hatch; no second lock is cut.
